description:
An integer-keyed bracket index PANICS THE COMPILER on run and build; interp is right.

  fn main() do
    m = %{1 => :one}
    dbg(m[1])
  end

  elixir      :one
  fz interp   :one
  fz run      panicked at src/compiler2/native_codegen/fn_ctx.rs:549:
              cannot coerce atom and numeric raw ABI reprs
  fz build    same panic; no binary produced

Narrowed: it needs an INTEGER KEY AND AN ATOM VALUE together.
  %{1 => "s"} / m[1]    -> "s"    on all three doors
  %{"k" => :v} / m["k"] -> :v     on all three doors

A compiler panic, not a diagnostic, and a three-door divergence. Pre-existing --
found while reviewing fz-5xp.4, whose decode of `m[1]` is byte-identical before
and after; codegen is untouched by that change.

Matters for this epic: fz-5xp.12 adds a real `Map`, and integer keys with atom
values are an ordinary shape (`%{1 => :ok}`).
title: Integer-keyed bracket index panics the compiler on run and build
